Tate Steel has identified a number of specific benefits that it sees from a combination with Corus. Enhanced scale will position the combined group as the fifth largest steel company in the world by production, with a meaningful presence in both Europe and Asia. The powerful combination of low cost upstream production in India with the high end downstream processing facilities of Corus will improve the competitiveness of the European operations of Corus significantly, The combination will also allow the cross-fertilisation of research and development capabilities in the automotive, packaging and construction sectors and there will be a transfer, from Europe to India of technology, best practices and expertise of senior Corus management. In addition, Tata Steel will retain access to low cost raw materials and slab for the enlarged group and exposure to high growth in emerging markets, whilst gaining price stability in developed markets. Tata Steel also believes that between the two companies, there exists a high degree of cultural compatibility which would facilitate an effective integration of the businesses over time. Tata Steel expects to lead the enlarged group with a combined management team. Manufacturing will be organized so as to produce slabs/primary steel in low-cost facilities and produce high-end products in proximity to client base-both Europe and India. Position high-end production in proximity to the client base-in both Europe and India. Tata Steel Limited has informed the Exchange that the Board of Directors at the Companay  at its meeting held on October 20, 2006, has approved acquisition of the entire issued share capital of Corus Group plc ("Corus") ("Acquisition"), at a price of 455 pence in cash for each share valuing Corus at GBP 4.3 billion. Corus is Europe's second largest steel producer with revenues in 2005 of GBP 9.2  billion, and crude steel production of 18.2 million tons primarily in U.K. and Netherlands. Corus is primarily engaged in the manufacture of semi-finished and finished carbon steel products. Its activities are divided in to three main divisions: strip products (including coated and uncoated strip and welded tubes, sold both as coil and sheet), long products (including sections, plates, wire rod, narrow strip and engineering steels) and the distribution and building systems division, which operates as a link between corus's manufacturing operation and its customers. It has a global network of sales offices and service centres. The Acquisition is proposed to be made by Tata Steel U.K. a wholly-owned indirect subsidiary of Tate Steel, recently incorporated  in the United Kingdom for the purpose of completing the Acquisition. The said Acquisition is proposed to be effected by means of a scheme of arrangement under Section 425 of the (English) Companies Act 1985 subject to High Court of Justice in England and Wales and Corus' shareholders approvals being obtained. Acquisition is proposed to be funded through its own cash resources and loans raised by Tata Steel and its subsidiary companies formed for the purpose of this acquisition. The Acquisition of Corus by Tata Steel is consistent with Tate Steel's stated objective of growth and globalization. Growth at Tata Steel has been focused towards new, higher end-markets and a more sophisticated customer base.

The investment was completed through a combination of preferential allotment of 24.99% equity shares to Tata Steel and 42.12% of equity shares through open tender offer.  The investment was made by the Company and its wholly owned subsidiary,  Natsteel Asia Pte Ltd, Singapore.  On conclusion of the above transaction, the Board of Millennium Steel was reconstituted with the majority of Directors being the nominees of Tata steel. Its Board comprises of 11 Directors of which 6 are the nominees of Tata Steel. Mr B Muthuraman Managing Director, Tata Steel has been appointed as the Chairman of Millennium Steel.  Other members of the Board are Dr. T. Mukherjee, Mr. U. K. Chaturvedi, Mr. Koushik Chatterjee and Mr. Oo Soon Hee. Mr. Santi Charnkolrawee, the present Managing Director of Millennium Steel would continue on the Board as a nominee of Tata Steel. Millennium Steel is one of the largest steel company in Thailand with a capacity of 1.7 mtpa, producing long products for construction and engineering steel for auto industry. It operates through 3 facilities in Thailand.

Tata Steel Limited has informed the Exchange that on March 13, 2006, Tata steel signed two external commercial borrowing agreements aggregating to Euro 61.42 Million (USD 73.36 Million) at Frankfurt. The above funding would be utilized to finance the import component of "Blast Furnace H" and "Sinter Plant 4" as part of the ongoing expansion project in Jamshedpur. "Blast Furnace H", which will produce 2.5 million tones per annum of hot metal, has been contracted to Paul Wurth Italia and Larsen & Toubro for commissioning. "Sinter Plant 4" of 2.3 million tones per annum capacity is contracted to Outokompu Technology GmbH, Germany and Larsen & Toubro. The ECA covered facilities were signed with Deutsche Bank Aktiengesellschaft, Frankfurt am Main as Original Lender. These facilities are insured by SACE S.p.A. (Servizi Assicurativi per il Commercio Estero ) of Italy and Euler HERMES Kreditversicherungs-Aktiengesellschaft of Germany. The loans have a repayment period of 10 years and an availability period of approximately three and two years respectively. The coupon on the loans will be Euribor plus 12 basis points. In the Financial Year 2005-06, Tata Steel has completed USD 971 Million of External Commercial Borrowings comprising of an IFC (& IFC Syndicated) Loan of USD 400 Million; a Sundicated Loan of USD 500 Million and the above ECA insured financing.

Tata Steel Limited has informed the Exchange that on March 07, 2006, Tata Steel signed an external commercial borrowing agreement of US$ 500 million (Japanese Yen equivalent of US$ 495 million and US$ 5 million) at Singapore, for funding its growth projects and acquisitions. The syndicated term loan facility was for US$ 400 million (or its equivalent in JPY) with a Greenshoe Option of further US$ 100 million (or its equivalent in JPY). 17 Banks across various geographies participated in the aforesaid syndicated term loan facility. The issue was oversubscribed and the Company exercised the Greenshoe Option. The loan has a door-to-door maturity of 7 years. The coupon of the loan will be Libor plus 45 basis points.

attchmntText: Tata Steel Limited has informed the Exchange that the Company on December 15, 2005 signed an agreement with Cementhai Holding Company, a Siam Cement Group Company, Thailand to acquire approximately 40% of Cementhai holding in Milliennium Steel, Thailand and to purchase an additional 24.9% by fresh issue of equity shares subject to shareholders approval. The Company will also undertake to proceed with an open offer subject to certain conditions precedent to be satisfied to Tata Steel requirements. 100% equity value of Millennium Steel Company as ascertained for the transaction is approximately US$ 175 million. Millennium Steel is one of the largest steel Company in Thailand, with a capacity of 1.7 mtpa, producing long products for construction and engineering steel for auto industry. It has three operating facilities in Saraburi, Rayong and Chonburi Province. For the year ended December 31, 2004, Millennium Steel recorded consolidated turnover of US$ 406 million and a net profit of US$ 29 million. The above transaction is subject to all regulatory approvals in Thailand and India as well as shareholders approval of Millennium Steel.

Tata Steel Limited had informed the Exchange that Tata Steel and BlueScope Steel have agreed to form a 50:50 Joint Venture Company in India. The Company has now informed the Exchange that the Company have on November 23, 2005 signed the Share Subscription Agreement and the Joint Venture Agreement with BlueScope Steel Limited, Australia, to form a 50:50 Joint Venture Company in India to manufacture zinc/aluminum metallic coated steel, painted metallic coated steel and rollformed steel products and deliver pre-engineered buildings and other building solutions. The Joint Venture will construct a new, state-of-the-art metallic coating and painting facility at Jamshedpur in Eastern India, adjacent to Tata Steel's existing steelworks. The new facility will have a metallic coating capacity of 250,000 tonnes and with a paint line capacity of 150,000 tonnes annually. The Joint Venture Company will invest capital cost of Rs.1,200 crores on four manufacturing locations in India and a network of sales offices across SAARC.

Tata Steel Limited has informed the Exchange that Tata Steel and BlueScope Steel have agreed to form a 50:50 Joint Venture Company in India. The joint venture company will build the business across India and South Asia that will manufacture zinc/aluminium metallic coated steel, painted metallic coated steel and rollformed steel products, and deliver pre-engineered buildings (PEB) and other building solutions. The Joint Venture Agreement will be officially signed at a ceremony later this month. The joint venture company will construct a major new, state-of-the-art metallic coating and painting facility at Jamshedpur. The new facility will have a metallic coating capacity of 250,000 tonnes and paint line capacity of 150,000 tonnes annually. The capital cost of the project will be approximately Rs. 900 crores. The investment is consistent with the Company's strategy of growing its downstream value-added products business. The joint venture company will assume ownership and responsibility for the development of the three rollforming and PEB manufacturing facilities which BlueScope Steel has under construction at Pune, Chennai and New Delhi. The joint venture will offer a comprehensive range of branded steel products for building and construction applications, including the premium ZINCALUME� and COLORBOND� coated steel, LYSAGHT� rollformed steel products and BUTLER PEBs. BlueScope Steel is the leading steel producer in Australia and New Zealand, supplying the majority of the flat steel products.

Tata Iron And Steel Co. Ltd. has informed the Exchange that the Government of Jharkhand and Tata Steel Limited on September 08, 2005, signed Memorandums of Understanding (MOUs) in respect of the setting up of new greenfield steel capacity and enhancement of capacity of Jamshedpur Works as under: (1) Setting up of a 12-million tonnes per annum greenfield integrated steel plant in Manoharpur and Chandil areas of Jharkhand with an estimated investment of Rs.42,000 crores. (2) Expansion of Tata Steel's existing plant at Jamshedpur from 5 million tones per annum to 10 million tonnes per annum with an estimated investment of Rs.11,000 crores. (3) Co-operation in the area of Human Resource Development thru Polytechnic. (4) Co-operation in the area of Human Resource Development thru Industrial Training Institute (ITI). The greenfield integrated steel plant of 12 mtpa will be set up in two phases. The project will also include the development of iron ore mines and other raw material sources including coal and logistic linkages for this plant. The expansion of Jamshedpur works from the present 5 mtpa to 10 mtpa will also be undertaken in two phases.  The Government of Jharkhand and Tata Steel have also entered into two separate MOUs to cooperate in the field of Human Resource Development with an objective to impart technical and job oriented training to the youth of the State through upgradation of polytechnics and Industrial Training Institutes with the help of expert assistance.

attchmntText: Tata Iron And Steel Co. Ltd. has informed the Exchange that the Company has on July 18, 2005, signed an agreement with AMCI Australia Pty. Ltd. to buy a 5% interest in the Carborough Downs Coal Project located in Queensland, Australia. The company also signed an offtake agreement for a proportion of the production over life of the project. Carborough Downs is an undeveloped underground coking coal project with production scheduled to commence in year 2006. It is located in Bowen Basin in Central Queensland. The project life is estimated to be of 14 years and approximately 58 million tones of raw coal is expected to be mined during this period. There is a further potential resource of 100 million tones of raw coal in the unexplored areas and deeper seams. The clean coal envisaged to be produced will be low-ash coking coal, highly suitable for steel making. The Carborough Downs coal project is majority owned and operated by AMCI Australia Pty. Ltd., a subsidiary of AMCI Holdings Australia Pty. Ltd. AMCI International AG, the apex holding company of AMCI Holdings Australia Pty. Ltd., is a large global producer, shipper and trader of high-grade metallurgical coal.

Tata Iron And Steel Co. Ltd. has informed the Exchange that the Company has on June 10, 2005, signed a Loan Agreement with International Finance Corporation (IFC) for availing loan of US $ 300 million. IFC is the private sector arm of the World Bank Group. The Company has further informed that under the agreement, IFC will provide Tata Steel with a corporate loan of US $ 300 million, which consists of an A-loan of US $ 100 million directly and a syndicated B-loan of US $ 200 million. The B-loan will be underwritten by Bank of America, N.A., Calyon, The Hongkong & Shanghai Banking Corporation Limited and Standard Chartered Bank. The IFC funding is an important part of Tata Steel's financing strategy. The IFC loan will help the Company to finance its future projects by way of long term funding.

Tata Iron And Steel Co. Ltd. has informed the Exchange that Tata Steel signed Joint Venture Agreements on June 12, 2005 with Iranian Mines and Mining Industries Development and Renovation Organizaton (IMIDRO) to join them in their proposed steel making projects and mining operations in Iran . Mr. M Moazenzadeh, Chairman of IMIDRO and Mr. B Muthuraman, Managing Director of Tata Steel signed the agreements in Tehran. Tata Steel would partner them in establishing a 1.5 mtpa (million tones per annum) steel slab making facility, a 1.5 mtpa of steel billet making capacity, a seperate 3 mtpa  export oriented steel plant and in exploraton & mining of unexplored iron ore mines. Tata Steel would partner  IMIDRO in the ongoing Hormozgan Steel project, which would establish  steel -making operations in the Persian Gulf Special Economic Zone (PGSEZ) at the port city of Bandar Abbas. The first phase of this gas based steel project would establish a 1.5 mtpa steel slab making facility, which would be followed by the second phase to establish 1.5 mtpa of steel billet making capacity. In a separate venture, Tata Steel would partner with IMIDRO in exploration and mining of unexplored iron ore mines at the Gol-e-Gohar mines in Kerman province of Iran and would establish a gas based pellet plant at Gol-e-Gohar using this iron ore. IMIDRO and Tata Steel also signed Memorandum Of Understanding expressing  Tata Steel's intent to establish a separate 3-mtpa export oriented  steel plant in two modules of 1.5 mtpa each at PGSEZ in Bandar Abbas in the vicinity of the Hormozgan steel plant.

Tata Iron And Steel Co. Ltd. has informed the Exchange that the Company signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on June 04, 2005 at Raipur, for setting up a 5 million tonnes per annum greenfield integrated steel plant in the Bastar region of Chhattisgarh. The MoU was signed by Mr. Shivraj Singh, Principal Secretary (Industries and Mineral Resources Department) on behalf of Government of Chhattisgarh and by Mr. B. Muthuraman, Managing Director, Tata Steel, in the presence of the Chief Minister of Chhattisgarh, Dr. Raman Singh and other Government dignitaries. According to the MoU, the integrated steel palnt will have an ultimate capacity of 5 million tonnes per annum of steel with 2 million tonnes per annum in first phase. The first phase of the steel plant is likely to be setup within 48 months to 60 months from the date of obtaining all statutory clearances. The project also includes development of captive iron ore mines to meet the iron ore requirements of this plant. The project is expected to generate employment, both direct and indirect, for large number of people.

Tata Iron And Steel Co. Ltd. had informed the Exchange regarding the shut down of 'G' Blast Furnace of the company at Jamshedpur.The company has now informed that the Company's largest blast furnace, 'G' has been blown in at 12.30 a.m. on  April 07, 2005. The G-Furnace, which had been shut down on December 03, 2004 for upgradation, had an initial capacity of one million tonnes per annum and a planned campaign life of 10 years. This furnace was blown out after producing a record 14 million tonnes in its first campaign of 12 years. The company has further informed that the upgraded furnace is designed to have a capacity of 1.80 mtpa, and a planned campaign life of 15 years. The furnace was upgraded at a cost of Rs. 580 crores, with the help from SMS-Demag, Germany and it is expected to produce better quality hot metal, at a lower fuel rate in the future. With this furnace in operation, the hot metal capacity of the Company would go up to 5.2 million tonnes in 2005-06, compared to a production of 4.35 million tonnes in 2004-05.

Tata Iron And Steel Co. Ltd. has informed the Exchange that the Company had entered into Definitive Share Subscription Agreement on August 16, 2004 to acquire 100% of the Steel Business of NatSteel Ltd. including the Singapore operations, investments in Thailand, China, Malaysia, Vietnam, Philippines and Australia. The company has completed the above transaction whereby the Company has subscribed to 100% equity of NatSteel Asia Pte Ltd. As part of the transaction, all steel assets of NatSteel Limited in Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Vietnam, Philippines, Australia and China (except Changzhou Wujin NatSteel) have been transferred to NatSteel Asia Pte Limited.  Amongst the China Investments the regulatory approvals for the transfer of Southern NatSteel (Xiamen) Co. Ltd. and Wuxi Jingyang Metal Products Co. Ltd. have been received and transferred to NatSteel Asia Pte Ltd. The transfer of Changzhou Wujin NatSteel Co. Ltd. to Natsteel Asia Pte Limited is delayed as the regulatory approval for Changzhou Wujin NatSteel Co. Ltd. is pending with the relevant authorities in China. Consequently, the Company has held back S$ 60 million from the purchase consideration for the above purpose. The Company has signed a Supplemental Subscription Agreement with NatSteel Ltd. on February 15, 2005 for the above purpose.  As per the Share Subscription Agreement signed on August 16, 2004, the Negotiated Enterprise Value was S$ 486.4 million and on completion Tata Steel was required to pay S$ 364.8 million (Initial Payment). The balance payment is subject to adjustment for Net Working Capital and other adjustments as will be determined by the Closing Audit. Pursuant to the Supplemental Subscription Agreement, the Company has held back S$ 60 million from the Initial Payment that would be released on successful transfer of Changzhou Wujin NatSteel Co. Ltd to NatSteel Asia Pte Ltd which is expected to be completed before the end of April 2005.

Tata Iron And Steel Co. Ltd. has informed the Exchange that on January 12, 2005, in the presence of Tata Group Chairman, Mr. Ratan Tata, the Chief Minister of West Bengal, Shri Budhadeb Bhattacharya and Mr. B Muthuraman, Managing Director of Tata Steel, the Company executed a Shareholders' Agreement in Kolkata with West Bengal Industrial Development Corporation Ltd. (WBIDC), to set up a Merchant Coke Oven Plant at Haldia. The proposed project is being undertaken to manufacture and sale of metallurgical coke in the international and domestic markets. This Plant will also supply coke to the Company's Works at Jamshedpur. The capacity of the coke oven plant will be 0.8 mil.tons of coke per year after Phase I. The Project has also envisaged generation of electric power of 60 MW capacity. During the same ceremony, a long term Power Purchase Agreement was also executed with West Bengal State Electricity Board. The capital cost of the project of around Rs.700 crores is proposed to be funded through a mix of debt & equity from Tata Steel and WBIDC.

Tata Iron And Steel Co. Ltd. has informed the Exchange that the company has on November 17,2004 signed a Memorandum of Understanding(MOU) with the Orissa Government for setting up a six million ton green field Steel Plant at Kalinganagar in Jaipur District of Orissa. According to the MOU,a six million ton Steel Plant will be set up at a total cost of Rs.15,400 crore in two modules of three million tons each. The first module, comprising three million ton steel plant complex having Blast Furnace, Coke Ovens, Sinter Plant, Caster and Rolling Mill will be completed in four years. This will be followed by the second module of three million ton to be set up in twenty four months thereafter. The project also includes development of captive iron ore mines to meet the iron ore requirements of this plant and modern townships for the employees of the Iron Ore Mines and the Steel Plant. The company has also drawn up plans for development of Gopalpur region, where it is in possession of 3200 acre land acquired by it for its earlier proposed Steel Plant. It proposed to set up a technical Training Institute at Goplapur and work with the State Government to help set up a Special Economic Zone(SEZ) on a part of the land. Pre feasibility study for setting up the SEZ has been completed and an SPV is now to be formed between Government of Orissa and the company to progress the matter further. The company also proposes to set up a cold Rolled Steel Processing Centre at Gopalpur, as part of forward integration of its Kalinganagar Steel Plant.

Tata Iron And Steel Co. Ltd. has informed the Exchange that the Company's Board has approved the signing of definitive agreements for its participation in the joint venture with L&T for the Dharma Port project in Orissa. The Agreements will be signed on October 29, 2004. Tata Steel's growth and globalization plans will leverage a modern deep-water port to bring down the logistics cost and provide greater accessibility to global markets. L&T's vast expertise in infrastructure projects and port construction will ensure the timely and economic completion of the port. The project cost as approved by the Board is around Rs.15 billion and will have a handling capacity of 25 million tones per annum. The project is planned over two phases and is expected to commence operations in Dec'2007. Third party cargo is also envisaged for this port.

Tata Iron And Steel Co. Ltd. has informed the Exchange that as part of the 1 million tonne per annum crude steel expansion programme at Jamshedpur, the Company has planned to reline and upgrade the capacity of 'G' Blast Furnace from the existing 1.2 million tonne per annum to 1.8 million tonne per annum. The 'G' Blast Furnace was earlier planned to be shut down for around 100 days from mid September 2004. The condition of the Blast Furnace was critically reviewed in the month of July 2004 and certain other steps were taken to prolong its life. These have been successful. Steps have also been taken to see that all other Blast Furnaces can produce full output during the revamping of 'G' Blast Furnace. It has thus been decided to shut down the furnace sometime in early December 2004 for 100 days. There will be no change in the overall production plan on account of the change in the shut down schedule.

Limited has vide its letter inter-alia stated, "In this connection, we would like to clarify that the Company, a leading user of IT, is an early adopter of SAP and it has implemented SAP in a phased manner to increase coverage of business processes and business units.
